title: EFFORT BATCH 28/29: (B) a forced failure of the host's new-game start - with a client ALREADY in the lobby - hands the host's lobby back, the client never starts (the host now runs its own New before telling anyone), and the SECOND Start starts both machines exactly once; (A+R2) the client's GenerateRivals, fed through the GenerateRivals transpiler after a per-start reset of the rival feed, mints exactly the host's 15 rival ids. The rig cannot run Proton - the field fault itself is not reproducible here
preconditions: Build with EFFORT BATCH 29 deployed (levers startfail [clientInLobby readout] + rivalids; charconfirm, hostnew existing). No fixture save is loaded - both machines generate a NEW world. The forced failure happens AFTER the client joined the lobby (batch 29 review R1). NOTHING is saved. The load-path failure is t-protonhost-load.
oracles_absent: called inside GenerateRivals but queue empty
a start is already in flight on this machine
oracles_report: sent to \d+ client\(s\) after the host's own start

steps.note: baseline: the client sits in the lobby

steps.expect_result: ^OK the next start continuation \(new game or host load\) throws once

expect_log.regex: \[Server\] StartNewGame error - lobby restored, Start can be pressed again: System.InvalidOperationException: DEV startfail lever

steps.note: FIRST press, client in the lobby: the host's continuation throws once BEFORE New - the failure is logged once and the latch is handed back
anything wrongly sent to the client would have landed by now
the lever fired once and the host's lobby is live again
THE R1 CHECK: the client was never told to start by the failed press (it is still in the lobby)

expect_log.regex: \[Server\] New game init \+ intro scene loaded
\[Server\] StartNewGame \(\w+\) sent to 1 client\(s\) after the host's own start; base cash \$\d+; rival ids \d+ rival\(s\)
\[Wave6\] GenerateRivals starting on client; UUID queue has 15 id\(s\)

steps.note: SECOND press: a real start on BOTH machines (the client's first and only start); the client's GenerateRivals runs from the host's 15-id feed re-sent behind its StartGameNew
both machines create characters (charconfirm) and settle
the host's own minted rival ids (7 wholesale + 8 import)
THE CHECK: the client's world holds the host's ids, in order (count 15)
report: the client settled into the new world
report: the client left the lobby once (the second start was acted on)
